subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser private-network confirmation, allow/block list, or temporary-grant policy, and what exact semantics should it use?
rationale: The proposal changes a security-sensitive browser egress boundary and public config/approval UX, so automation should not choose prompt, timeout, metadata hard-deny, audit, redirect, or migration semantics.

options.title: Approve a staged browser SSRF policy
options.body: Define hard metadata blocks, allow/block list rules, timeout/rate/audit behavior, redirect handling, and upgrade compatibility before implementing the narrow approved phase.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to a user-approval UX with session state and timeout semantics across all browser navigation and redirect paths before implementation.

options.title: Keep current static policy
options.body: Leave browser SSRF as strict default plus host exceptions and broad trusted-environment opt-in, and close this only after maintainers decide not to expand core policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a staged browser SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Define hard metadata blocks, allow/block list rules, timeout/rate/audit behavior, redirect handling, and upgrade compatibility before implementing the narrow approved phase.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current source, docs, and adjacent security-policy history for this browser SSRF surface.
